## A practical layer for active teaching {background-color="#052048" .title-slide}

<div class="title-grid">

<div class="title-copy">
<div class="subhead">Pulse links attendance, participation and transparent records</div>

One browser-based service supports teachers during class and gives students a simple, privacy-conscious way to join, check in, claim points and view an anonymous league.

**This deck has three sections**

## The teaching problem

<div class="two-col wide-gap">

<div class="big-statement">
Attendance and participation often live in separate spreadsheets, paper lists and personal notes.
</div>

<div class="clean-list">
- Classroom actions must take seconds, not minutes.
- Students need a clear explanation of what data the service records.
- Multiple teachers need a shared view of a course.
- Corrections must preserve history rather than erase it.
- Administrative and IT teams need a deployable, auditable service.
</div>

</div>

## The service model

<div class="flow five">

<div class="flow-node">
<b>1</b><strong>Course roster</strong><small>Teacher imports institutional student records</small>
</div>

<div class="flow-node">
<b>2</b><strong>Course joining</strong><small>Each student activates their place once</small>
</div>

<div class="flow-node">
<b>3</b><strong>Class attendance</strong><small>Short-lived QR records presence</small>
</div>

<div class="flow-node">
<b>4</b><strong>Participation</strong><small>QR claims or direct teacher awards</small>
</div>

<div class="flow-node">
<b>5</b><strong>Records</strong><small>Private tables, corrections and exports</small>
</div>

</div>

## What each audience receives

| Audience | Primary value | Typical interaction |
|---|---|---|
| Students | A consistent way to join, check in and receive participation credit | Mobile browser and QR scan |
| Teachers | Fast classroom controls and one course record | Teacher dashboard |
| Course teams | Shared operational visibility across teachers | Course membership and audit records |
| University administration | Evidence of engagement processes and accountable corrections | Aggregated exports and governance controls |
| IT and information security | A small web service with explicit data stores, secrets and deployment requirements | Hosting, identity, monitoring and backup |

## Student and teacher journeys

<div class="journey-pair">

<div class="journey student">
<div class="subhead">Student</div>
<ol><li>Scan the permanent course joining QR</li><li>Enter a student number and choose an animal nickname</li><li>Scan a class attendance QR</li><li>Claim participation points when invited</li><li>Check personal totals and the anonymous league</li></ol>
</div>

<div class="journey teacher">
<div class="subhead">Teacher</div>
<ol><li>Create or open a course</li><li>Import the roster and timetable</li><li>Open a scheduled or ad hoc class</li><li>Show attendance or points QR codes</li><li>Award selected students directly when needed</li><li>Review, correct and export records</li></ol>
</div>

</div>

## Participation points are course evidence

<div class="two-col">

<div class="clean-list">
<div class="subhead">Two award routes</div>

**QR claim**  
The teacher defines points, context, audience and validity. Eligible students scan and claim once.

**Direct teacher award**  
The teacher selects one or more enrolled students. The students do not scan and do not need to have joined the app.
</div>

<div class="source-ledger">
<div><span>QR</span><strong>Student claim</strong><small>Source identifies a QR award</small></div>
<div><span>TD</span><strong>Teacher direct</strong><small>Source identifies the awarding teacher</small></div>
<div><span>↺</span><strong>Correction</strong><small>Reversal remains linked to the original event</small></div>
</div>

</div>

## Privacy and identity boundaries

<div class="boundary-grid">

<div class="boundary good">
<div class="subhead">Current safeguards</div>
- Course access for teachers
- Anonymous public league labels
- One claim per eligible student
- Expiring attendance and award tokens
- Auditable corrections
- Read-only reviewer account option
</div>

<div class="boundary caution">
<div class="subhead">Pilot limitations</div>
- Student number entry does not prove institutional identity
- Small cohorts can weaken practical anonymity
- Teacher access still uses pilot access codes
- Institutional retention and grading policy remain governance decisions
</div>

</div>

<div class="notes">
Do not describe the pilot as a finished identity solution. Production migration should connect teacher and student identity to university systems and apply the approved retention policy.
</div>

## Data held by the service

<div class="data-map">

<div><strong>Course joining</strong><span>Activation time and chosen anonymous nickname</span></div>
<div><strong>Attendance</strong><span>Class, time, source, verification state and correction status</span></div>
<div><strong>Points</strong><span>Amount, reason, class context, source, teacher and reversals</span></div>
<div><strong>Operations</strong><span>Courses, teaching team, timetable and session state</span></div>
</div>

## Deployment and integration view

<div class="architecture">
<div class="actor">Student browser</div>
<div class="actor">Teacher browser</div>

## Production-readiness decisions

<div class="decision-list">
<div><b>Identity</b><span>Map institutional staff and student identities to course roles.</span></div>
<div><b>Data protection</b><span>Approve lawful basis, notices, retention, subject rights and incident handling.</span></div>
<div><b>Hosting</b><span>Define service owner, environments, secrets, backups, monitoring and recovery targets.</span></div>
<div><b>Teaching policy</b><span>Decide how participation points relate to assessment and reasonable adjustments.</span></div>
<div><b>Support</b><span>Publish routes for access problems, incorrect records and classroom contingencies.</span></div>
</div>

## Evidence and reporting

<div class="two-col">

<div class="clean-list">
<div class="subhead">Teacher-facing evidence</div>
- Chronological events
- Course totals and rankings
- Attendance records
- Current enrolments
- Point source and awarding teacher
- Corrections without deleting originals
</div>

<div class="clean-list">
<div class="subhead">Export options</div>
- CSV for each course table
- Checked-in student export
- Course backup export
- Data suitable for local reconciliation and approved downstream analysis
</div>

</div>

## Roster import checks

<div class="two-col">

<div class="clean-list">
<div class="subhead">Before import</div>
- Use the required participant filename and CSV structure.
- Confirm the target course shown in the preview.
- Review rows marked new, update or error.
- Correct missing IDs, names or invalid email values.
</div>

<div class="callout caution">
<div class="subhead">Replace roster requires care</div>
Replacement removes absent students from the active course roster while preserving historical attendance and points. Use it only when the file represents the intended complete roster.
</div>

</div>

## Opening and closing classes

<div class="screen-layout">

<div class="app-window narrow-screen">
<div class="app-top"><span class="app-logo">P</span><b>Pulse</b><small>SEMESTER CLASSES</small></div>
<div class="schedule"><div><small>T03 · 16 SEP · 14:00</small><strong>Sampling distributions</strong><span>Room 2.3.14</span><button>Open class</button></div><div class="complete"><small>T02 · COMPLETED</small><strong>Probability review</strong><span>Previous session retained</span><button>Reset to scheduled</button></div></div>
</div>

<div class="screen-notes">
**Open class** starts the selected scheduled class.

**Close session** ends attendance and class-limited award QR codes.

**Reset to scheduled** makes a test class available again without deleting its previous records.
</div>

</div>

## Direct teacher award

<div class="screen-layout">

<div class="app-window award-window">
<div class="app-top"><span class="app-logo">P</span><b>Participation award</b></div>
<div class="award-form"><div class="tabs"><span>QR code</span><b>Award directly</b></div><label>Count points toward<select><option>Independent coursework (no class)</option></select></label><div class="point-row"><button>+1</button><button class="selected">+2</button><button>+3</button><button>+5</button></div><label>Reason<input value="Coursework submitted on Moodle" readonly></label><label>Find students<input value="Search by name or student number" readonly></label><div class="student-pick"><span>☑ Ana Student <small>fc12345</small></span><span>☐ Bruno Student <small>fc23456</small></span></div><button class="primary">Award 2 points to 1 student</button></div>
</div>

<div class="screen-notes">
The course landing page exposes **Select students directly** separately from QR creation.

Direct awards work for any enrolled student, even if the student has not joined the app.

The audit record stores the direct source and awarding teacher.
</div>

</div>

## Choosing the right award route

| Situation | Recommended route | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| A live question answered during class | Short-lived QR | Students claim immediately and only once |
| A small group completes a classroom task | Restricted QR | Only selected joined students can claim |
| Coursework arrives by email or Moodle | Direct teacher award | No student scan needed |
| A teacher notices a missing award later | Direct teacher award | Clear teacher attribution and reason |
| A previous award was incorrect | Reverse in course records | Preserves the original and the correction |

## End-of-class routine

<div class="end-routine">
<div><span>01</span><strong>Check the room list</strong><small>Resolve obvious missing attendance while the class context is fresh.</small></div>
<div><span>02</span><strong>Close the session</strong><small>This ends attendance and class-limited award codes.</small></div>
<div><span>03</span><strong>Review recent activity</strong><small>Confirm attendance and participation events.</small></div>
<div><span>04</span><strong>Correct when needed</strong><small>Record a reason so the audit history remains intelligible.</small></div>
</div>

## Teacher contingencies

<div class="two-col">

<div class="clean-list">
<div class="subhead">If a QR fails</div>
- Confirm that the student joined the course.
- Check that the code has not expired or been deactivated.
- Generate a new code if the original validity ended.
- Use a direct award for a documented participation event.
</div>

<div class="clean-list">
<div class="subhead">If a student cannot check in</div>
- Confirm that the student number matches the roster.
- Check the class and course shown on screen.
- Add a missing attendance record from Course Data when justified.
- Record a clear correction reason.
</div>

</div>

# Student guide {background-color="#397785" .section-slide}

## What students need

<div class="student-needs">
<div><span>1</span><strong>A phone or computer browser</strong><small>No app-store installation is required.</small></div>

<div><span>3</span><strong>The QR shown by the teacher</strong><small>Joining, attendance and points use different codes.</small></div>
</div>

## Attendance check-in

<div class="student-action">
<div class="large-number">01</div><div><strong>Scan the attendance QR during class</strong><span>The QR identifies the current class and expires after the teacher’s chosen period.</span></div>
<div class="large-number">02</div><div><strong>Enter the roster student number</strong><span>Pulse checks that the number belongs to this course.</span></div>
<div class="large-number">03</div><div><strong>Read the confirmation</strong><span>A successful screen confirms the recorded class.</span></div>
</div>

## Claiming QR points

<div class="screen-layout">

<div class="phone wide-phone">
<div class="phone-top">Pulse · Participation</div><div class="success-icon">✓</div><h4>Claim 2 points</h4><p>Insightful answer</p><label>Student number<input value="fc12345" readonly></label><button>Claim points</button><small>Each eligible student can claim once.</small>
</div>

<div class="screen-notes">
The reason and number of points appear before confirmation.

Some QR codes work for every joined student. Others accept only students selected by the teacher.

If the QR expired, ask the teacher whether they intend to generate another code.
</div>

</div>

## Direct awards need no student action

<div class="big-statement centered">
When a teacher awards points directly, the student does not scan a QR.
</div>

The course total updates from the teacher’s recorded award. Typical examples include coursework sent by email, work submitted in Moodle or a missing classroom award corrected later.

## Student troubleshooting

<div class="faq">
<div><strong>“Student not found”</strong><span>Use the student number on the course roster, not an email address. Ask the teacher to check the import if it still fails.</span></div>
<div><strong>“Already claimed”</strong><span>Each award QR allows one successful claim per eligible student.</span></div>
<div><strong>“QR expired”</strong><span>The validity period ended or the teacher closed the class or deactivated the award.</span></div>
<div><strong>Wrong attendance or points</strong><span>Contact the teaching team. Teachers can correct the record while preserving the audit history.</span></div>
</div>

## Responsible classroom use

<div class="boundary-grid">

<div class="boundary good">
<div class="subhead">Students</div>
- Use only your own student number.
- Do not share active QR links outside the intended class.
- Check confirmations before closing the page.
- Report incorrect records promptly.
</div>

<div class="boundary good">
<div class="subhead">Teachers</div>
- Explain the purpose of attendance and points.
- Avoid displaying personal student records publicly.
- Use meaningful reasons for direct awards and corrections.
- Apply the agreed course policy consistently.
</div>

</div>

## Recommended rollout

<div class="timeline">
<div><b>Pilot</b><span>Confirm teaching workflow, support load and student understanding with synthetic or low-stakes use.</span></div>
<div><b>Institutional integration</b><span>Connect SSO, course membership and approved hosting. Complete privacy and security actions.</span></div>
<div><b>Controlled adoption</b><span>Train teaching teams, publish student guidance and monitor service indicators.</span></div>
<div><b>Review</b><span>Evaluate educational value, accessibility, data quality and operational cost before wider use.</span></div>
</div>

## Ownership and next decisions

<div class="ownership">
